sourcePolicy: Only official university or university-system admissions pages are accepted.

records.fact: ACT/SAT not required for admission or merit scholarship; scores may be submitted optionally.
SAT or ACT required for first-year admission; Caltech uses section-level bucket review for fall 2027 applicants.
ACT or SAT required for Columbus first-year applicants, with exceptions for applicants out of high school two or more years; superscoring is used.
Test-optional for spring, summer and fall 2027; scores are optional for admission, Honors College and merit scholarship consideration.
Test-free: SAT/ACT are not used in admission, holistic review or scholarship decisions; they may be used for placement or subject credit after admission.
UC system test-free policy applies: SAT/ACT are not considered for admission or scholarships; they may be used for eligibility alternatives or placement after enrollment.
UC system test-free policy applies: SAT/ACT are not considered for admission or scholarships; they may be used for eligibility alternatives or placement after enrollment.
SAT/ACT are not considered for admission or scholarship purposes; they may be used for eligibility alternatives or placement after enrollment.
UC system test-free policy applies: SAT/ACT are not considered for admission or scholarships; they may be used for eligibility alternatives or placement after enrollment.
UC system test-free policy applies: SAT/ACT are not considered for admission or scholarships; they may be used for eligibility alternatives or placement after enrollment.
UC system test-free policy applies: SAT/ACT are not considered for admission or scholarships; they may be used for eligibility alternatives or placement after enrollment.
UC system test-free policy applies: SAT/ACT are not considered for admission or scholarships; they may be used for eligibility alternatives or placement after enrollment.
UC system test-free policy applies: SAT/ACT are not considered for admission or scholarships; they may be used for eligibility alternatives or placement after enrollment.
SAT or ACT required; exceptional applicants without access may use AP, IB, GCSE/A-Level or national leaving exam results/predictions.
SAT or ACT required for first-year and transfer applicants; ACT writing/science and SAT essay are not required.
ACT or SAT required for first-year and transfer applicants; no minimum score and no preferred exam.
Test-optional for undergraduate first-year and transfer applicants; submitted scores may be considered, but are not required.
Test-optional for applicants enrolling fall 2027; SAT/ACT requirement returns for fall 2028 applicants.
SAT or ACT required for first-year applicants; SAT Essay, ACT Writing and ACT Science are optional.
SAT or ACT required for first-year applicants; transfer applicants do not need SAT/ACT.
Test-optional for the 2026-27 admission cycle; requirement returns for fall 2028 applicants.
Standardized testing requirement reactivated for undergraduate applicants beginning with the Class of 2029.
SAT and/or ACT submission required; Georgetown does not accept superscores and does not consider ACT Writing.
Standardized testing or a testing waiver required for undergraduate applicants beginning with the 2025-26 admissions cycle.
ACT or SAT required for first-year and transfer applicants; ACT Science and Writing are optional.
Test-optional for first-year and transfer applicants in the 2026-27 admissions cycle; submitted scores may be considered.
Test-optional for applicants entering fall 2027 or 2028; testing required for fall 2029 and later.
ACT/SAT optional through spring 2028, including fall 2027; not considered for transfer admission.
Freshman applicants must send at least one official SAT, ACT or qualifying CLT score; SAT Essay, ACT Writing and ACT Science are not required.
All first-year applicants must submit at least one SAT or ACT score; ACT Writing and SAT Essay are not required.
Test-optional for the 2027 application cycle; applicants may choose whether SAT/ACT are considered.
Test-optional for fall 2027 first-year applicants; transfer remains test-optional.
SAT/ACT not required; scores are generally not seen in review, though very high scores may help a small number of applicants; international English proficiency remains required.
SAT/ACT recommended but not required for first-year and transfer applicants; submitted scores may be considered.
Standardized testing is not required for NYU applicants; applicants may submit SAT, ACT, AP, IB or accepted international exams under the test-flexible policy.
Test-optional for first-year applicants entering fall 2027; submitted SAT/ACT scores may be self-reported and reviewed.
Test-optional through fall 2028 and spring 2029 for all undergraduate schools and scholarship programs; submitted scores may be reviewed.
Test-optional for undergraduate admission; international applicants still need English-proficiency evidence unless an official waiver applies.

For fall 2026 applicants, testing varies by college: required for the School of Computer Science, optional for the College of Fine Arts, and test-flexible for Engineering, Dietrich, Heinz Information Systems, Mellon College of Science and Tepper.
Test-optional for first-year and transfer applicants; applicants whose first language is not English must provide official English-proficiency results unless an exception applies.
Test-optional for first-year and transfer applicants; non-native English-speaking applicants must demonstrate English proficiency through an approved test or an official waiver process.

Test-optional for undergraduate applicants; applicants whose primary language is not English must show English proficiency unless they completed at least three years in an English-instruction secondary school.
Test-optional for IU Bloomington; applicants choose whether SAT/ACT scores are considered, and merit scholarship opportunities remain available with or without scores.

SAT or ACT is required for first-year applicants; English-proficiency tests are recommended for applicants whose primary language is not English or who have not attended an English-language school for the last three years.
Test-optional for first-year applicants for the 2027-28 academic year; international applicants whose native language is not English must still demonstrate English proficiency.
All first-year applicants must submit official ACT or SAT scores under the University System of Georgia policy; international applicants must also demonstrate English proficiency.

All first-year applicants must submit an ACT, CLT or SAT score; international applicants are evaluated under the same freshman process and must meet the required testing and English-proficiency conditions.
Test-optional through Spring and Fall 2027; non-native English speakers still need approved English-proficiency scores or an approved waiver.
ACT/SAT is optional through Fall 2029; international applicants and other applicants who meet the language criteria must demonstrate English proficiency, with alternate waiver routes available.

Test-optional through the 2026-27 academic year; Notre Dame will reinstate SAT/ACT requirements for applicants seeking Fall 2028 enrollment. International applicants may still need English-proficiency testing.

Undergraduate admission is test-optional and submitted scores are not required for admission or scholarship consideration; international applicants must submit English-proficiency scores or request a waiver.

WashU requires English-proficiency testing for international students whose second language is English; beginning with Fall 2027 applicants, SAT/ACT will no longer substitute for that English-proficiency requirement.
Test-optional for undergraduate applicants; international applicants may need approved English-proficiency results, and SAT/ACT may be used as an English-proficiency option.

SAT/ACT requirements are suspended through the 2026-27 cycle; international applicants who do not submit SAT/ACT must submit an approved English-proficiency exam unless their school uses English as the primary language of instruction.

Test-optional for first-year admission; SAT/ACT scores are not required, but applicants may self-report them for consideration. International applicants must separately meet English-proficiency requirements.
Test-optional for undergraduate applicants; UChicago applies a no-harm policy when considering submitted SAT or ACT scores.
Test-optional for general admission; ACT/SAT may be required for some scholarships, English-proficiency pathways, or program-specific conditions, and submitted scores are used under a no-harm policy.
ACT/SAT optional for all first-year applicants, including international students; applicants may choose whether scores are considered, while English-proficiency rules still apply when required.
Test-optional for undergraduate admission; no testing is required for undergraduate programs or scholarships, and applicants choose whether to submit SAT/ACT scores.
Test-optional for first-year admission; SAT/ACT scores are not required and applicants are not penalized for withholding them. Non-native English speakers must provide English-proficiency evidence.

Test-optional for first-year applicants with weighted GPA of 2.8 or above; applicants below that threshold may need SAT, ACT or CLT scores, and international applicants may submit scores but are not required to.

Purdue accepts SAT, ACT or CLT scores and expects first-year applicants to provide test scores in the normal application; exceptional applicants who could not take a test may still submit an application without one. International applicants must separately prove English proficiency.

First-year applicants must submit at least one ACT, CLT or SAT score under Florida Board of Governors requirements; international applicants must also provide English-proficiency evidence. A limited Florida AA pathway is exempt from the test-score requirement.

Test-optional for students applying for Fall 2027; SAT/ACT will be required again for the Fall 2028 application cycle. International applicants still need an approved English-proficiency test unless an exception applies.
Test-optional for Rutgers–New Brunswick undergraduate applicants through 2027; submitting SAT/ACT is optional and applicants who do not submit scores receive full admission consideration.

Standardized test scores are not required for admission; applicants may self-report or submit SAT/ACT scores for consideration. International applicants must provide approved English-proficiency evidence unless exempt.
Test-optional for undergraduate admission indefinitely; applicants decide whether SAT/ACT scores are included, and all applicants are considered for merit programs regardless of score submission.
Test-optional for undergraduate admission; applicants may choose whether SAT/ACT scores are included in holistic review.
Test-optional for first-year applicants; SAT/ACT submission is optional, and UConn superscores submitted results while excluding writing and science sections from review.
Test-optional for all first-year applicants; submitting SAT/ACT is optional and choosing not to submit does not negatively affect holistic admission or merit consideration.
SAT/ACT test-optional for first-year and transfer applicants through Fall 2029, with exceptions including Accelerated Pre-Medicine and Pre-Law programs, which require test scores.

Standardized tests are optional for first-year applicants across all majors; UMass Amherst reviews applications with or without SAT/ACT scores and still considers applicants for merit scholarships without scores.

Test-optional for most undergraduate applicants; SAT/ACT is required for the B.A./B.S.-M.D. program, homeschool applicants, and applicants from schools using only narrative evaluations. Scores are not required for merit scholarships.
Test-optional for undergraduate admission; applicants may submit SAT/ACT scores, and applicants without scores remain eligible for admission, scholarships, and honors programs.

Test-optional for first-year applicants; applicants choose whether ACT/SAT scores are included, and students applying without scores remain eligible for merit scholarships. International students may use ACT/SAT for English proficiency but are not required to submit them for admission.
SAT/ACT not required for undergraduate admission; submitted scores may be considered, and applicants who apply test-optional are not disadvantaged in admission or scholarship review.

Fully test-optional for undergraduate admission; no preference is given based on whether scores are submitted, and applicants without scores remain eligible for admission, scholarships and honors consideration.
Test-optional for first-year applicants; students choose whether SAT/ACT scores are considered, and Stony Brook uses holistic review. Some scholars programs may have separate score requirements.
SAT/ACT not required for applicants entering Fall 2026, Spring 2027, Fall 2027 or Spring 2028; applicants without scores are not disadvantaged and remain eligible for merit scholarships.
Test-optional for first-year admission; applicants are not required to submit SAT/ACT scores, while submitted scores may be considered and superscored.
Test-optional for undergraduate admission; applicants decide whether SAT/ACT scores are considered, and choosing not to submit scores does not negatively affect review.

Test-optional for undergraduate admission; applicants choose whether SAT/ACT scores are considered, and all applicants remain eligible for merit scholarships and academic programs regardless of score submission.
SAT/ACT optional for Fall 2027 first-year and transfer admission; scores are required for the invitation-only Pathways to Medicine program and are preferred for some academic merit scholarships.

SAT/ACT scores are optional for first-time freshman admission; top-quarter and second-quarter applicants can receive guaranteed admission without scores, while lower-ranked applicants may use scores in secondary review. Scores are encouraged for advising, placement and some scholarships.
For entry from Fall 2026 onward, applicants with weighted GPA below 2.8 must submit ACT 17+ or SAT 930+; applicants with weighted GPA 2.8 or higher may choose whether to self-report SAT/ACT scores.

Test-optional for first-year applicants entering through Fall 2028; SAT/ACT submission is optional, applicants remain eligible for scholarships without scores, and English-proficiency testing is still required where applicable.

Test-optional for undergraduate applicants through the Fall 2030 application cycle; applicants choose whether SAT/ACT scores are considered. The Physician-Scientist B.S./M.D. program requires official scores.
Test-optional for first-year applicants; applicants may choose whether SAT/ACT scores are considered, and submitted scores are superscored.

Test-optional for first-year admission; beginning with the 2027 cycle, submitted ACT/SAT scores are considered only when they positively contribute to the application. Applicants without scores receive full holistic consideration and remain eligible for merit scholarships.
Test-optional through the 2026-27 admission campaign (Class of 2031); applicants may choose whether SAT/ACT scores are considered and will not be disadvantaged without scores.
Penn State Behrend follows Penn State's test-optional admission policy; SAT/ACT scores are not required for admission, but applicants may submit them for consideration.

Test-optional through the 2027-28 application cycle; applicants choose whether SAT/ACT scores are considered, and applicants without scores remain eligible for merit scholarships. English proficiency is separately required where applicable.

For the current undergraduate admission policy, SAT/ACT scores are considered for first-year applicants; the official bulletin identifies test-optional admission specifically for performance-based Frost School of Music applicants, while non-native English speakers must submit English-proficiency scores. The prior COVID-era test-optional window covered Fall 2025 and Spring 2026.

Pitt-Bradford is test-optional for new students; applicants may submit SAT/ACT scores, and only scores that benefit the student factor into the admission decision. Certain programs may have separate requirements.

For Fall 2027 first-year admission, the University of Iowa uses a no-harm test policy: applicants may apply without ACT/SAT scores, and submitted scores are used only when they benefit admission or scholarship review. International applicants who completed secondary school outside the United States generally do not need ACT/SAT scores for admission, but scores may be required for scholarships, certain direct-admission programs, or the Honors Program; English-proficiency requirements remain separate.
